description: Gemini zodiac sign: personality traits, strengths and challenges, love, career, decans and dates (May 21 to June 20).
answer: In Western astrology, Gemini is the third sign of the zodiac, a mutable air sign ruled by Mercury. It is traditionally associated with curiosity, wit, adaptability and a quick, talkative mind. The Sun is in Gemini from about May 21 to June 20. The exact dates shift by a day from year to year.

sections.heading: Gemini personality traits
paragraphs: Gemini is the sign of the Twins, and the image hints at its most recognisable trait: more than one way of seeing anything. A Gemini mind tends to run several conversations at once, picking up a fact from a podcast, a phrase from a stranger and an idea from an old novel, then connecting them in ways nobody else spotted. Curiosity is the engine. This sign is often described as the eternal student, forever asking why and slightly distracted by the next interesting thing. From outside that can look like inconsistency, but it usually reflects a genuine hunger to understand how the world, and especially how people, actually work.

In the language of astrology, Gemini is a mutable air sign ruled by Mercury. Air is the element of thought, communication and social exchange; mutable signs sit at the end of a season and specialise in adapting, translating and moving between states. Mercury, the messenger, governs language, trade, travel and the nervous system. Combine the three and you get a sign that lives through words and connections, comfortable with change, quick to learn and happiest when there is something new to discuss. Gemini traditionally rules siblings, neighbours and short journeys, which suits its fondness for local networks, friendly gossip and plenty of daily variety.

sections.heading: Gemini strengths and challenges
paragraphs: Gemini's chief asset is agility. It can usually grasp a new subject quickly, adjust its approach mid-stream and chat with almost anyone, from a toddler to a chief executive, in a way that puts them at ease. Humour is often a major gift; the Twins tend to be playful with language and quick with a well-timed remark. This is a natural connector, introducing friends, swapping recommendations and keeping information moving through a group. Its open-mindedness means it rarely clings to a position out of pride, and it can revise a view gracefully when new evidence arrives. In a world that keeps shifting, that flexibility is real and underrated.

Scattered attention is the classic Gemini struggle. With so many interests competing, depth can be sacrificed for breadth, and commitments may be dropped when something shinier appears. Gemini can talk its way around a feeling rather than through it, using wit or analysis to keep emotional intensity at arm's length. Others sometimes experience this as superficiality or unreliability, even when the intention is kind. Restlessness can also feed nervous tension, overcommitment and trouble switching off at night. And because the Twins enjoy seeing every side, they may hesitate to take a firm stand, leaving people unsure where they truly sit on things that matter.

sections.heading: Gemini in love and relationships
paragraphs: For Gemini, attraction usually starts in the mind. Someone who can keep up with its banter, surprise it with an idea or open the door to an unfamiliar world will hold its interest far longer than someone offering chemistry alone. Gemini brings fun, conversation and lightness to a relationship; life alongside the Twins rarely feels stale. Affection tends to arrive as attention: messages through the day, private jokes, a plan to try that new place together. What this sign asks for is room to keep its own friendships and interests, plus a partner who does not read its sociability as a lack of loyalty.

Difficulty tends to arise when emotional depth is called for and Gemini reaches for distraction instead. A partner may feel that serious conversations get deflected or that commitment is perpetually postponed. The Twins, meanwhile, can feel suffocated by heavy expectations or rigid routine. Naming feelings in words helps, since language is Gemini's home ground, and so does agreeing on a few non-negotiable rituals of connection amid all the variety. Keeping the relationship curious, through travel, new hobbies and long late-night talks, feeds the bond. Libra and Aquarius are traditionally seen as kindred spirits, while Aries and Leo bring the spark Gemini enjoys.

sections.heading: Gemini at work
paragraphs: Gemini tends to thrive in work that rewards communication, variety and quick thinking. Journalism, teaching, marketing, sales, public relations, broadcasting, writing, translation and technology all suit it, as does any role built on negotiation or networking. It often prefers juggling several projects to grinding away at one, and it can be the person who spots links between departments or ideas that specialists miss. In charge, Gemini usually leads through persuasion and ideas rather than rank, keeping meetings lively and everyone informed. Its openness to feedback and readiness to pivot make it well suited to fast-moving industries where last month's plan rarely survives intact.

The main pitfalls are focus and finishing. Gemini can launch many initiatives and complete few, or spread itself so thin that quality suffers. Routine admin may bore it into procrastination. With money, the Twins are often inventive about earning, running side projects or several income streams at once, but they may also spend on a whim, particularly on gadgets, books, courses and trips. A light system that tracks what comes in and goes out, glanced at briefly but regularly, tends to outlast an elaborate budget that gets abandoned by March. Partnering with a methodical colleague can turn Gemini's brilliant beginnings into finished, polished results.

sections.heading: Growth and the three Gemini decans
paragraphs: Gemini's growth edge is depth. A worthwhile experiment is choosing one subject, skill or friendship and deliberately staying with it past the point of novelty, to discover what lies beneath the first exciting layer. Journaling can help, because writing gives a busy mind a way to slow down and catch feelings it might otherwise talk past. Building in quiet stretches without screens or input lets an overstimulated nervous system settle. In relationships, practising listening without preparing a reply can be quietly transformative. It also helps to make fewer promises and keep every one of them, so that the Twins' many talents come with a reputation for doing what they said they would do.

Gemini divides into three decans of ten degrees each. The first, roughly May 21 to May 30, belongs to Mercury; the second, about May 31 to June 10, to Venus; and the third, around June 11 to June 20, to Uranus. Each has its own page, and every Gemini birthday links to its decan.

faq.question: Are Geminis two-faced?
faq.answer: The two-faced label is an unfair reading of the symbol. The Twins represent versatility and the ability to hold several perspectives at once. Gemini can seem changeable because it adapts quickly and loves exploring ideas, not usually because it is being dishonest with anyone.

faq.question: What careers suit Gemini?
faq.answer: Roles built on communication and variety tend to fit best: writing, teaching, journalism, marketing, sales, media and technology. Gemini usually does well where it can keep learning, talk with many different people and move between projects rather than repeating one task all day.

faq.question: What are the dates for Gemini?
faq.answer: About May 21 to June 20. The Sun's entry into each sign moves by a day or so between years, so birthdays at either end are cusp dates; the zodiac sign calculator settles them for a specific year.

faq.question: What are the three Gemini decans?
faq.answer: The first decan (0° to 9°) is linked with Mercury, the second (10° to 19°) with Venus and the third (20° to 29°) with Uranus, following the rulers of the air signs in zodiac order.
